To determine the number of different complementary three-card sets in a deck of 27 cards where each card has a unique combination of shape, color, and shade, we need to consider the rules for complementary sets. A set is complementary if for each attribute (shape, color, shade), the three cards are either all the same or all different.

We can use the concept of lines in affine geometry. The deck of cards can be considered as a 3-dimensional affine space over the finite field GF(3). Each card corresponds to a point in this space, and a complementary set corresponds to a line (1-flat) in this space.

The formula for the number of lines in an n-dimensional affine space AG(n, 3) is given by:
\[
\frac{3^{n-1} \cdot (3^n - 1)}{2}
\]

For our problem, n = 3 (shape, color, shade). Plugging into the formula:
\[
\frac{3^{3-1} \cdot (3^3 - 1)}{2} = \frac{3^2 \cdot (27 - 1)}{2} = \frac{9 \cdot 26}{2} = 9 \cdot 13 = 117
\]

Thus, the number of different complementary three-card sets is \boxed{117}.
